38942638.exclusion_reason: Broad annual survey of Canadian radiology practice/policy topics; AI for pediatric brain tumors mentioned only briefly among many unrelated topics.

38950412.exclusion_reason: Clinician survey using AI-generated case scenarios; not itself an imaging AI or radiology diagnostic study (AI used only to generate the vignettes).

38961684.clinical_problem: Using a deep learning decision-support algorithm to identify pediatric pneumothorax or pleural effusion on chest X-rays and determine whether tube thoracostomy is warranted.
38961684.model_description: XRAInet, a deep learning algorithm, takes pediatric chest radiographs as input and localizes regions of pneumothorax/pleural effusion, classifying whether tube thoracostomy intervention is warranted versus conservative management.
38961684.headline_result: mAP 0.918; independent test set sensitivity 64.00%, specificity 96.15%

38967815.model_family: AI image reconstruction (vendor algorithm, architecture unspecified)
38967815.clinical_problem: Improving image quality and reducing scan time for pediatric brain MRI using AI-based image reconstruction at higher acceleration factors.
38967815.patient_population: 50 pediatric patients (mean age 11.8±3.1 years) undergoing clinical brain MRI
38967815.model_description: An AI reconstruction algorithm processes accelerated (higher compressed-SENSE factor) 3D T1-weighted SPGR brain MRI acquisitions and reconstructs images with improved signal-to-noise and contrast-to-noise ratios compared to standard reconstruction.
38967815.headline_result: AI improved image quality in 94-100% of evaluations at CS=5/8; significantly higher aSNR/aCNR (p<0.001)

39004418.clinical_problem: Using unsupervised machine learning clustering of CMR-derived ventricular dyssynchrony metrics to identify high-risk phenotypes among patients with Fontan circulation for single-ventricle congenital heart disease.
39004418.patient_population: 503 CMR studies from Fontan patients (median age 15y) and 42 age-matched controls, single center, 2005-2011
39004418.model_description: Unsupervised K-means clustering machine learning applied to 24 CMR-derived mechanical dyssynchrony metrics (from feature-tracking strain analysis) classifies Fontan patients into distinct phenotypic risk clusters associated with death or heart transplantation.
39004418.headline_result: Highest-risk cluster HR 6.4 (95% CI 2.1-19.3) for composite outcome vs lowest-risk cluster
39004418.study_design: retrospective single-center cohort study with unsupervised machine learning

39022236.model_family: deep learning image reconstruction (DLIR) + MAR algorithm
39022236.clinical_problem: Reducing metal-induced beam-hardening artifacts from pedicle screws on post-surgical pediatric low-radiation-dose spine CT, using metal artifact reduction combined with deep learning image reconstruction.
39022236.model_description: Deep learning image reconstruction (DLIR) combined with a metal artifact reduction (MAR) algorithm processes low-dose post-surgical pediatric spine CT raw data to reduce beam-hardening artifacts around pedicle screws and improve image quality, compared to iterative reconstruction (ASIR-V).
39022236.headline_result: DL-MAR reduced artifact length by 57.4% and artifact index by 65.0% vs standard reconstruction

39028358.clinical_problem: Automated classification of ADHD from resting-state functional MRI activity patterns using a 3D convolutional neural network, to support decision-support systems for diagnosis.
39028358.patient_population: ADHD-200 database (NeuroImage, NYU, Peking University cohorts), children/adolescents
39028358.model_description: A 3D convolutional neural network takes fractional amplitude of low-frequency fluctuations (fALFF) and regional homogeneity (ReHo) fMRI-derived features as input and classifies individuals as ADHD or typically developing, using the public ADHD-200 dataset.
39028358.study_design: retrospective multi-site public-dataset model development and cross-site validation study

39033342.model_family: logistic regression with genetic algorithm feature selection
39033342.clinical_problem: Using MRI-derived morphological measurements and machine learning to identify anatomic risk factors for patellofemoral (patellar) instability in children and adolescents.
39033342.patient_population: 54 pediatric patients with acute lateral patellar dislocation, 54 age-matched controls (2005-2022)
39033342.model_description: Machine learning and genetic algorithm optimization applied to MRI-derived patellofemoral, tibial, tibiofemoral and patellar height morphological parameters build a logistic regression model predicting risk of lateral patellar dislocation.
39033342.headline_result: Optimized logistic regression model AUC 0.934; KS index alone AUC 0.87

39115097.exclusion_reason: Wearable pressure/EMG sensor engineering study for scoliosis brace monitoring; Cobb angle prediction is from sensor data, not radiologic imaging, and deep learning is a minor component.

39143994.clinical_problem: Using CT radiomics features of the spleen to noninvasively differentiate Burkitt lymphoma from lymphoblastic lymphoma in children.
39143994.patient_population: 48 patients with lymphoblastic lymphoma, 61 with Burkitt lymphoma (109 total pediatric patients)
39143994.model_description: Radiomics features extracted from splenic CT images (noncontrast, arterial, venous phases) are combined via classifiers (QDA, LR, SVM) into fusion models to differentiate Burkitt lymphoma from lymphoblastic lymphoma.

39152998.clinical_problem: Antenatal MRI-based radiomic prediction of severe placenta accreta spectrum (placenta increta) to guide delivery planning.
39152998.patient_population: 100 women with placenta accreta spectrum (mean age 34.6±3.9), 64 with placenta increta, multi-center 2018-2023
39152998.model_description: Radiomic features extracted from T2-weighted antenatal MRI, combined with a clinical variable, are used in a random forest/support vector machine classifier to predict severe (increta) placenta accreta spectrum subtype.
39152998.headline_result: Clinical-radiomic model AUC 0.713, accuracy 0.695, sensitivity 0.843, specificity 0.447
39152998.study_design: multi-center retrospective radiomics model validation study

39190703.clinical_problem: Evaluating whether deep-learning-based MR image reconstruction techniques alter quantitative radiomic features extracted from abdominal organs, relevant to radiomics-based pediatric and adult imaging research reliability.
39190703.patient_population: 17 pediatric and adult subjects, prospective abdominal MRI
39190703.model_description: Two deep-learning-based MR image reconstruction algorithms (SmartSpeed, SmartSpeed-SuperRes) are compared against conventional reconstruction (C-SENSE) for their effect on 86 quantitative radiomic features extracted from abdominal organ regions of interest.
39190703.dataset_size: 17 pediatric and adult subjects, 86 radiomic features, 8 ROIs
39190703.headline_result: 50/86 features highly correlated (PCC>=0.8) SmartSpeed vs C-SENSE; only 15/86 for SmartSpeed-SuperRes

39212832.clinical_problem: Evaluating deep-learning-based image reconstruction (CIRIM) versus compressed sensing for accelerated 3D FLAIR brain MRI in patients with neurological deficits, including pediatric patients.
39212832.patient_population: 62 patients with neurological deficits (mixed pediatric/adult); plus 451 public FastMRI FLAIR scans for acceleration-factor analysis
39212832.model_description: CIRIM (Cascades of Independently Recurrent Inference Machines), a deep-learning reconstruction algorithm, reconstructs 12-fold accelerated 3D T2-FLAIR brain MRI, compared against compressed sensing reconstruction by neuroradiologists (including a pediatric neuroradiologist).
39212832.dataset_size: 62 patients (12-fold accelerated 3D FLAIR); 451 public FastMRI FLAIR scans
39212832.headline_result: CIRIM 28% higher SNR, 5x faster than CS; radiologists preferred CIRIM for artifacts/conspicuity/contrast (p<0.01)
39212832.study_design: prospective reader study comparing reconstruction algorithms

39260859.body_region: fetal (Doppler, gestational age/growth) and maternal (blood pressure)
39260859.clinical_problem: Prospectively evaluating AI/deep-learning analysis of low-cost one-dimensional Doppler ultrasound signals to automatically detect fetal growth restriction, pre-eclampsia and hypertension in a resource-limited setting.
39260859.patient_population: 700 pregnant women, rural Guatemala, protocol study
39260859.model_description: Deep-learning algorithms process 1-D Doppler ultrasound signals of fetal heart tones to estimate fetal gestational age, intrauterine growth, and maternal blood pressure, for automated screening of fetal growth restriction and pre-eclampsia.

39264983.clinical_problem: Automated scoliosis screening and Cobb angle estimation from upright back photographs to reduce unnecessary radiography in adolescents.
39264983.patient_population: 247 scoliosis patients (2008-2021), frontal/lateral/back images and X-rays
39264983.model_description: Deep learning algorithms localize the back region of interest, segment the spinal region, and estimate Cobb angle from upright back photographs, validated against traditional radiographic measurement.
39264983.headline_result: Cobb angle measurement accuracy superior to traditional human visual recognition method (specific number not stated)

39283409.clinical_problem: Automated quantification of hip migration percentage from pelvis radiographs to support hip surveillance and severity assessment in children with cerebral palsy.
39283409.patient_population: 210 patients (children with cerebral palsy), X-ray scans
39283409.model_description: Machine learning landmark-detection models (fine-tuned VGG-19 with pre-trained weights) take anterior-posterior pelvis radiographs as input and predict hip landmarks used by a geometric algorithm to automatically calculate migration percentage for hip dysplasia severity assessment.
39283409.headline_result: VGG-19 fine-tuned model achieved lowest MSE for landmark detection (specific error value not stated)

39294484.clinical_problem: Discussing the potential for AI to improve diagnostic accuracy for skull fractures and brain hemorrhages in pediatric head trauma, and to reduce need for repeat imaging.
39294484.patient_population: Children with minor head trauma, particularly under 24 months (commentary)
39294484.model_description: Editorial commentary discussing AI models for detecting skull fractures and brain hemorrhages on CT/MRI in pediatric head trauma, referencing reported accuracy improvement from 78.1% to 85.2%.
39294484.headline_result: AI improved diagnostic accuracy from 78.1% to 85.2%, reduced errors 2-3 fold (as cited)

39307122.clinical_problem: Using AI-based automatic brain segmentation and machine learning on structural MRI to quantify brain structural abnormalities and diagnose autism spectrum disorder in children.
39307122.patient_population: 60 ASD children, 48 typically developing children, prospectively enrolled Jan 2023-Apr 2024
39307122.model_description: Automated AI brain segmentation technique measures standardized volumes of brain structures from 3D-T1 MRI, and machine learning classifiers (SVM, AdaBoost, etc.) use these volumes to diagnose ASD versus typical development.
39307122.headline_result: SVM AUC 0.91, AdaBoost AUC 0.92 for ASD classification

39335401.clinical_problem: Using functional MRI and machine learning (SVM) to characterize longitudinal changes in reading-related brain activity patterns in medulloblastoma survivors compared with healthy controls.
39335401.patient_population: Medulloblastoma survivors and controls, longitudinal study over three annual visits (N not specified)
39335401.model_description: Support vector machine classification applied to functional MRI data acquired during rapid automatized naming tasks distinguishes brain activity patterns of medulloblastoma survivors from healthy controls over three longitudinal visits.

39382534.clinical_problem: Evaluating performance of computer-aided detection systems for lung nodules on standard-dose versus low-dose pediatric chest CT.
39382534.model_description: Two publicly available lung nodule CAD systems (FlyerScan, MONAI), originally trained on adult data, process pediatric standard-dose and low-dose chest CT scans to detect and localize pulmonary nodules 3-30mm.
39382534.release_evidence: "FlyerScan (github.com/rhardie1/FlyerScanCT) and Medical Open Network for Artificial Intelligence (MONAI; github.com/Project-MONAI/model-zoo/releases)"

39407181.clinical_problem: Using deep learning analysis of chest radiographs to differentiate atrial septal defect from ventricular septal defect in children, given their distinct treatments.
39407181.model_description: Four deep learning network models (ResNet-CBAM, InceptionV3, EfficientNet, ViT) take pediatric chest radiographs as input and classify septal defect type (ASD vs VSD), compared against radiologist interpretation.
39407181.headline_result: InceptionV3 best AUC 0.91, 87% classification accuracy, exceeding radiologists
39407181.study_design: retrospective five-fold cross-validation model development and reader comparison study

39440041.clinical_problem: Automated deep-learning diagnosis of biliary atresia from gallbladder ultrasound images in neonates to improve diagnostic efficiency and accuracy.
39440041.patient_population: Neonates; thousands of gallbladder ultrasound images
39440041.model_description: GallScopeNet, a deep learning model with advanced feature extraction, takes gallbladder ultrasound images as input and classifies cases as biliary atresia or non-biliary atresia.
39440041.dataset_size: thousands of ultrasound images (majority train/val, subset external test)
39440041.study_design: retrospective model development with external testing

39442245.clinical_problem: Developing a multi-site-robust deep learning framework to diagnose autism spectrum disorder from functional MRI connectivity data, addressing scanner/site variability that limits generalizability.
39442245.model_description: CCMSMCF, a deep learning framework combining multi-head cross-attention and multi-context modules, takes multi-site fMRI functional connectivity data as input and classifies ASD versus typical development while remaining robust to scanner/site variability.
